key_insight: In de novo Parkinson’s disease, cognitive decline appears to reflect accelerated neurodegeneration layered on top of pre-existing white matter hyperintensity (WMH)-related vascular vulnerability, rather than faster WMH accumulation over time.
clinical_relevance: This suggests that both brain atrophy patterns and vascular burden may help identify patients at higher risk for faster multidomain progression in PD.
method: Newly diagnosed, untreated PD participants from PPMI who were cognitively normal at baseline were followed for at least 3 years.
Linear mixed-effects models tested longitudinal changes in cognition, MRI atrophy, WMHs, and clinical outcomes.
Joint models assessed how baseline WMH burden and an atrophy-pattern expression score related to later multidomain progression.
evidence_signal: In 350 participants, 58 converted to cognitive decline and showed faster worsening across cognitive, motor, gait, neuropsychiatric, sleep, and functional measures; baseline WMH burden and atrophy-pattern expression were both associated with subsequent progression across multiple outcomes.
watch_item: The findings are observational and based on model associations, so they support risk stratification rather than proving that WMHs or atrophy directly cause progression.
paper_title: Vascular and neurodegenerative contributions to cognitive decline and multidomain progression in de novo Parkinsons disease
